demo_out=[list(map(int,l.split())) for l in out_demo.splitlines()]
code='''from collections import Counter, deque

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    seen=set(); blocks=[]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c] == bg or (r,c) in seen: continue
            q=deque([(r,c)]); seen.add((r,c)); cells=[]
            while q:
                y,x=q.popleft(); cells.append((y,x))
                for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    yy,xx=y+dy,x+dx
                    if 0<=yy<h and 0<=xx<w and grid[yy][xx]!=bg and (yy,xx) not in seen:
                        seen.add((yy,xx)); q.append((yy,xx))
            y0=min(y for y,x in cells); y1=max(y for y,x in cells)
            x0=min(x for y,x in cells); x1=max(x for y,x in cells)
            counts=Counter(grid[y][x] for y,x in cells)
            color,n=counts.most_common(1)[0]
            area=(y1-y0+1)*(x1-x0+1)
            # Large, nearly solid rectangular components are the objects; all other marks are noise.
            if area>=4 and n>=4 and n/area>=0.65:
                blocks.append((y0,y1,x0,x1,color))
    out=[[bg]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for y0,y1,x0,x1,color in blocks:
        for y in range(y0,y1+1):
            for x in range(x0,x1+1): out[y][x]=color
    return out
'''
